The staged rendering of the same verse names him as well, and the unit's English quotation of 40:5 is cut back to its closing sentence, so the rendering that would have exposed the error is the part not shown. The claim is therefore false in both witnesses and contradicted by the unit's own quoted evidence, and it carries an unanchored positional forward reference to the unit that follows on top of that. High severity is right. The apparatus item is also upheld: the paseq inventory records a seg at MT 40:1, inside Jer.40.1-Jer.40.5, and the unit discloses the ketiv/qere at MT 40:3 and the preceding setumah at MT 39:18, so the layer is engaged and the sweep is owed across the span. The quote-fidelity item is upheld and under-counted: three marks are degraded, not two - the opening mark of the embedded speech in the web:Jer.40.2 rendering, and in the web:Jer.40.4 rendering both the contraction in 'don't' and the closing mark after 'go there'. Sound and to be preserved: the header's membership in the eleven-verse superscription shape is byte-correct at oshb:Jer.40.1, carrying the aleph-lamed form rather than the one-site variant; disclosing that the shape frames a release narrative rather than sermon content, instead of letting the formula name the unit, is the right handling and should survive the repair; and the renderings of web:Jer.40.1, web:Jer.40.5 and web:Jer.40.6 are character-exact, the 40:5 one at a live continuation-fold verse.
docket.remedy: Three orders. (1) In device_notes, strike the claim that Gedaliah is not yet named in this stretch; if the kinship observation is kept at all, re-cut it to the bytes - both the personal name and the two-generation patronymic stand at oshb:Jer.40.5 - and verse-anchor any forward reference instead of naming the unit that follows; test: every name-presence claim is checkable against the unit's own splice and against the staged rendering of the cited verse, which is the check the original fails. (2) In boundary_rationale, disclose the paseq at MT 40:1, single-witness, seg-layer, count-only, with no intra-verse position asserted; test: the span's paseq inventory is swept, not spot-cited. (3) In boundary_rationale, restore the three staged marks in the web:Jer.40.2 and web:Jer.40.4 renderings; test: each quoted run matches the staged verse text character-for-character with no straightening applied.

current_row.boundary_rationale: The unit opens on the prose-sermon superscription shape, הַדָּבָ֞ר אֲשֶׁר הָיָ֤ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֨הוּ֙ מֵאֵ֣ת יְהוָ֔ה אַחַ֣ר שַׁלַּ֣ח אֹת֗וֹ נְבוּזַרְאֲדָ֛ן רַב טַבָּחִ֖ים מִן הָֽרָמָ֑ה בְּקַחְתּ֣וֹ אֹת֗וֹ וְהֽוּא אָס֤וּר בָּֽאזִקִּים֙ בְּת֨וֹךְ כָּל גָּל֤וּת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ וִֽיהוּדָ֔ה הַמֻּגְלִ֖ים בָּבֶֽלָה (oshb:Jer.40.1, byte), matching “The word which came to Jeremiah from Yahweh, after Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard had let him go from Ramah, when he had taken him being bound in chains among all the captives of Jerusalem and Judah who were carried away captive to Babylon.” (web:Jer.40.1) — here the formula frames not a sermon from Yahweh's own mouth but Jeremiah's release, so the header's SHAPE is disclosed as a deviation from its usual prose-sermon content rather than silently relabeled. The captain of the guard becomes the scene's own speaker at once, וַיִּקַּ֥ח רַב טַבָּחִ֖ים לְיִרְמְיָ֑הוּ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֔יו יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֗יךָ דִּבֶּר֙ אֶת הָרָעָ֣ה הַזֹּ֔את אֶל הַמָּק֖וֹם הַזֶּֽה (oshb:Jer.40.2, byte), matching “The captain of the guard took Jeremiah and said to him, "Yahweh your God pronounced this evil on this place;” (web:Jer.40.2), and his theological reading of the disaster continues without any addressee change through וַיָּבֵ֥א וַיַּ֛עַשׂ יְהוָ֖ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֵּ֑ר כִּֽי חֲטָאתֶ֤ם לַֽיהוָה֙ וְלֹֽא שְׁמַעְתֶּ֣ם בְּקוֹל֔וֹ וְהָיָ֥ה לָכֶ֖ם דבר הַדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה (oshb:Jer.40.3, byte); a ketiv דבר stands against qere הַדָּבָ֥ר at oshb:Jer.40.3 (single-witness). Nebuzaradan's offer of a free choice closes on וְעַתָּ֞ה הִנֵּ֧ה פִתַּחְתִּ֣יךָ הַיּ֗וֹם מִֽן הָאזִקִּים֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל יָדֶךָ֒ אִם ט֨וֹב בְּעֵינֶ֜יךָ לָב֧וֹא אִתִּ֣י בָבֶ֗ל בֹּ֚א וְאָשִׂ֤ים אֶת עֵינִי֙ עָלֶ֔יךָ וְאִם רַ֧ע בְּעֵינֶ֛יךָ לָבֽוֹא אִתִּ֥י בָבֶ֖ל חֲדָ֑ל רְאֵה֙ כָּל הָאָ֣רֶץ לְפָנֶ֔יךָ אֶל ט֨וֹב וְאֶל הַיָּשָׁ֧ר בְּעֵינֶ֛יךָ לָלֶ֥כֶת שָׁ֖מָּה לֵֽךְ (oshb:Jer.40.4, byte), matching “Now, behold, I release you today from the chains which are on your hand. If it seems good to you to come with me into Babylon, come, and I will take care of you; but if it seems bad to you to come with me into Babylon, don't. Behold, all the land is before you. Where it seems good and right to you to go, go there."” (web:Jer.40.4). His advice that Jeremiah go to Gedaliah continues at once, וְעוֹדֶ֣נּוּ לֹֽא יָשׁ֗וּב וְשֻׁ֡בָה אֶל גְּדַלְיָ֣ה בֶן אֲחִיקָ֣ם בֶּן שָׁפָ֡ן אֲשֶׁר֩ הִפְקִ֨יד מֶֽלֶךְ בָּבֶ֜ל בְּעָרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֗ה וְשֵׁ֤ב אִתּוֹ֙ בְּת֣וֹךְ הָעָ֔ם א֠וֹ אֶל כָּל הַיָּשָׁ֧ר בְּעֵינֶ֛יךָ לָלֶ֖כֶת לֵ֑ךְ וַיִּתֶּן ל֧וֹ רַב טַבָּחִ֛ים אֲרֻחָ֥ה וּמַשְׂאֵ֖ת וַֽיְשַׁלְּחֵֽהוּ (oshb:Jer.40.5, byte); it closes on Jeremiah's actual release, matching “So the captain of the guard gave him food and a present, and let him go.” (web:Jer.40.5), with no new speaker or addressee marking a seam anywhere inside this stretch. a setumah closes oshb:Jer.39.18 (WLC, single-witness; weak, tier-3 corroboration under the Prophets addendum), closing the preceding narrative immediately before this span's own opening. Jeremiah himself moves scenes at the very next verse, וַיָּבֹ֧א יִרְמְיָ֛הוּ אֶל גְּדַלְיָ֥ה בֶן אֲחִיקָ֖ם הַמִּצְפָּ֑תָה וַיֵּ֤שֶׁב אִתּוֹ֙ בְּת֣וֹךְ הָעָ֔ם הַנִּשְׁאָרִ֖ים בָּאָֽרֶץ (oshb:Jer.40.6, byte), matching “Then Jeremiah went to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam to Mizpah, and lived with him among the people who were left in the land.” (web:Jer.40.6), where a fresh location marks the turn, and this unit stops short of that turn.

current_row.boundary_rationale: The subject widens from Jeremiah himself to the field captains as a group, וַיִּשְׁמְעוּ֩ כָל שָׂרֵ֨י הַחֲיָלִ֜ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּשָּׂדֶ֗ה הֵ֚מָּה וְאַנְשֵׁיהֶ֔ם כִּֽי הִפְקִ֧יד מֶֽלֶךְ בָּבֶ֛ל אֶת גְּדַלְיָ֥הוּ בֶן אֲחִיקָ֖ם בָּאָ֑רֶץ וְכִ֣י הִפְקִ֣יד אִתּ֗וֹ אֲנָשִׁ֤ים וְנָשִׁים֙ וָטָ֔ף וּמִדַּלַּ֣ת הָאָ֔רֶץ מֵאֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא הָגְל֖וּ בָּבֶֽלָה (oshb:Jer.40.7, byte), matching “Now when all the captains of the forces who were in the fields, even they and their men, heard that the king of Babylon had made Gedaliah the son of Ahikam governor in the land, and had committed to him men, women, children, and of the poorest of the land, of those who were not carried away captive to Babylon,” (web:Jer.40.7); the parashah layer marks oshb:Jer.40.6 with a setumah (single-witness; the Prophets addendum holds this tier-3 weak, disclosed rather than argued as a driver), closing the preceding notice immediately before this span's own opening. Named figures enter at once, including oshb:Jer.40.8 carries its own ketiv/qere pair: עופי written, עֵיפַ֣י read (single-witness), וַיָּבֹ֥אוּ אֶל גְּדַלְיָ֖ה הַמִּצְפָּ֑תָה וְיִשְׁמָעֵ֣אל בֶּן נְתַנְיָ֡הוּ וְיוֹחָנָ֣ן וְיוֹנָתָ֣ן בְּנֵֽי קָ֠רֵחַ וּשְׂרָיָ֨ה בֶן תַּנְחֻ֜מֶת וּבְנֵ֣י עופי עֵיפַ֣י הַנְּטֹפָתִ֗י וִֽיזַנְיָ֨הוּ֙ בֶּן הַמַּ֣עֲכָתִ֔י הֵ֖מָּה וְאַנְשֵׁיהֶֽם (oshb:Jer.40.8, byte), matching “then Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, and Johanan and Jonathan the sons of Kareah, and Seraiah the son of Tanhumeth, and the sons of Ephai the Netophathite, and Jezaniah the son of the Maacathite, they and their men came to Gedaliah to Mizpah.” (web:Jer.40.8); a paseq also falls at this verse (single-witness, seg layer, count-only). Gedaliah becomes the scene's own speaker without any further address change, opening on a sworn assurance rather than a divine formula, וַיִּשָּׁבַ֨ע לָהֶ֜ם גְּדַלְיָ֨הוּ בֶן אֲחִיקָ֤ם בֶּן שָׁפָן֙ וּלְאַנְשֵׁיהֶ֣ם לֵאמֹ֔ר אַל תִּֽירְא֖וּ מֵעֲב֣וֹד הַכַּשְׂדִּ֑ים שְׁב֣וּ בָאָ֗רֶץ וְעִבְד֛וּ אֶת מֶ֥לֶךְ בָּבֶ֖ל וְיִיטַ֥ב לָכֶֽם (oshb:Jer.40.9, byte), matching “Gedaliah the son of Ahikam the son of Shaphan swore to them and to their men, saying, "Don't be afraid to serve the Chaldeans. Dwell in the land, and serve the king of Babylon, and it will be well with you.” (web:Jer.40.9). It closes on his own instruction to settle the land, וַאֲנִ֗י הִנְנִ֤י יֹשֵׁב֙ בַּמִּצְפָּ֔ה לַֽעֲמֹד֙ לִפְנֵ֣י הַכַּשְׂדִּ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָבֹ֖אוּ אֵלֵ֑ינוּ וְאַתֶּ֡ם אִסְפוּ֩ יַ֨יִן וְקַ֜יִץ וְשֶׁ֗מֶן וְשִׂ֨מוּ֙ בִּכְלֵיכֶ֔ם וּשְׁב֖וּ בְּעָרֵיכֶ֥ם אֲשֶׁר תְּפַשְׂתֶּֽם (oshb:Jer.40.10, byte), matching “As for me, behold, I will dwell at Mizpah, to stand before the Chaldeans who will come to us; but you, gather wine and summer fruits and oil, and put them in your vessels, and dwell in your cities that you have taken."” (web:Jer.40.10). A different party — Jews scattered in Moab, Ammon, and Edom, rather than the captains already gathered at Mizpah — opens the next report at oshb:Jer.40.11, and this unit does not reach that turn.

docket.grounds: The recurrence half is upheld on the bytes; the front-seam half is narrowed. The unit's closing verse carries the two-item יַ֥יִן וָקַ֖יִץ (oshb:Jer.40.12, byte tier), while the verse named as the source of the recurrence carries a three-item list, יַ֨יִן וְקַ֜יִץ וְשֶׁ֗מֶן (oshb:Jer.40.10, byte tier), matching “gather wine and summer fruits and oil” (web:Jer.40.10). The oshb:Jer.40.10 form is spliced in no field of the unit and the recurrence carries no tier label, so a sameness claim stands with no quoted form behind it and on the wrong count object, a pairing named for a three-item list. The front-seam half is narrowed rather than upheld as framed: calling the incoming population unconnected to the captains is byte-true about who the group is, since the Jews in Moab, Ammon and Edom are not the field captains, so the bytes do not contradict it. What is defective there is a disclosure gap of the same class the unit elsewhere honours: its own onset verse opens on the additive particle וְגַ֣ם (oshb:Jer.40.11, byte tier), rendered “Likewise” (web:Jer.40.11), a byte-true continuity signal standing directly across the unit's own front seam and left undisclosed while a different cross-seam device is disclosed.
